spots.name: Inverness Castle

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Inverness Castle is a castle overlooking the River Ness in Inverness, Highland, Scotland. A succession of castles has occupied the site since 1057, although the present red sandstone structure was completed in 1836 to designs by William Burn and later extended by Thomas Brown II.

spots.name: Inverness Cathedral
spots.summary: Inverness Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral Church of Saint Andrew (1866–69), is a cathedral of the Scottish Episcopal Church situated in the city of Inverness in Scotland close to the banks of the River Ness.

spots.name: Old High St Stephen's

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Old High St Stephen's Church is a parish church of the Church of Scotland in Inverness, the capital city of the Highlands of Scotland. The congregation was formed on 30 October 2003 by a union of the congregations of Inverness Old High (57.4801°N 4.2289°W) and Inverness St Stephen's (57.4730°N 4.2186°W).

spots.name: Kessock Bridge
spots.summary: The Kessock Bridge carries the A9 trunk road across the Beauly Firth at Inverness, Scotland.

spots.name: Inverness Town Steeple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Inverness Town Steeple, formerly known as the Inverness Tolbooth, is all that remains of the former tolbooth on the High Street in Inverness, Scotland. The building, which is currently used to accommodate a private business, is Category A listed.

spots.name: Inverness Museum and Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Inverness Museum and Art Gallery is a museum and gallery on Castle Wynd in Inverness in the Highlands of Scotland. There is no entry charge. The collection and facilities are managed by High Life Highland on behalf of Highland Council.

spots.name: Greig Street Bridge
spots.summary: Greig Street Bridge is a footbridge across the River Ness located in Inverness, Scotland. It is a suspension bridge built in 1880–1 by the civil engineer C. Manners in conjunction with the Rose Street Foundry for a cost of £1,400.

spots.name: Inverness Town House
spots.summary: Inverness Town House is a municipal building in the High Street, Inverness, Scotland. The town hall, which was the headquarters of Inverness Town Council and now serves as a local office of the Highland Council, is a Category A listed building.

spots.name: St Mary's, Inverness

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mary's, Inverness is a Roman Catholic church in the city of Inverness, Inverness-shire, in Scotland and is a part of the Diocese of Aberdeen. The building is significant for the high quality of its altar and stained glass windows.

spots.name: East Church, Inverness

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: East Church, Inverness is a Category B listed building and former parish church of the Church of Scotland in Inverness.

spots.name: Tomnahurich Cemetery
spots.summary: The Tomnahurich Cemetery is a Victorian cemetery lying on and around a wooded hill in Inverness, Scotland.

spots.name: Eden Court Theatre
spots.summary: Eden Court Theatre is a large theatre, cinema and arts venue situated in Inverness, Scotland close to the banks of the River Ness.

spots.name: Highland Council Headquarters
spots.summary: The Highland Council Headquarters, formerly County Buildings, is a municipal structure in Glenurquhart Road, Inverness, Highland, Scotland. The oldest part of the complex, which currently serves as the headquarters of the Highland Council, is a Category C listed building.

spots.name: Rose Street Foundry
spots.summary: Rose Street Foundry was an industrial facility established in Rose Street, Inverness in the 1830s. It was the property of the Inverness Iron Company until 1872 when the Northern Agricultural Implement and Foundry Company Limited was established to take over the Inverness Iron Company.

spots.name: Cameron Barracks
spots.summary: Cameron Barracks is a British Army installation that stands on Knockentinnel Hill on the eastern outskirts of Inverness in Scotland.

spots.name: Craig Phadrig
spots.summary: Craig Phadrig is a forested hill on the western edge of Inverness, Scotland. A hill fort on the summit is generally supposed to have been the base of the Pictish king Bridei mac Maelchon.

spots.name: Caledonian Stadium
spots.summary: Caledonian Stadium, currently known as the Sarens PSG Stadium for sponsorship reasons, is a football stadium in the Longman area of Inverness, Scotland, near the banks of the Moray Firth. It is the home ground of Scottish Championship club Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

spots.name: ShipSpace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: ShipSpace was an interactive maritime museum in Inverness, Scotland. The museum was situated along the historic Caledonian Canal at the Muirtown Basin.

spots.name: Crown Church, Inverness

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Crown Church is a parish church in Inverness in the Scottish Highlands, located at the junction of Midmills Road and Kingsmills Road near the city centre.

spots.name: Filter Bunker Raigmore Inverness
spots.summary: The Filter Bunker Raigmore Inverness is the one remaining of a group of three subterranean bunkers situated around Raigmore in Inverness, Scotland. All three bunkers were constructed around 1940 for use by the Royal Air Force to process RADAR signals from Chain Home masts.

spots.name: Telford Street Park
spots.summary: Telford Street Park was a football ground in Inverness, Scotland. It was the home ground of Caledonian F.C. and latterly Caledonian Thistle F.C.

spots.name: Abertarff House, 71 Church Street, Inverness

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: Built in 1593, the oldest house in Inverness, now run by the National Trust for Scotland, with a small exhibition and garden.

spots.summary: Its denizens are mostly 19th-century, but the original Chapel of St Mary, part of a monastery, was 14th-century. Chapel and monastery are long gone as Cromwell carried off the masonry to build a bastion.
